target.title: Disambiguate duplicate session titles
target.body:
Closes #954.

## What Problem This Solves

The Sessions page rendered raw gateway display names, so forked or otherwise colliding sessions could be indistinguishable.

## Summary

- Reuse one session-title formatter across native chat and the Sessions page.
- Add deterministic numeric suffixes when key-derived qualifiers still collide, without exposing raw session keys.
- Preserve the original session keys for navigation and actions.

## Validation

- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~SessionTitleFormatterTests|FullyQualifiedName~OpenClawChatDataProviderTests'`: 234 passed.
- `dotnet build ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj -c Debug -r win-x64 --no-restore`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- GitHub Actions Windows matrix: 8 passed, 4 expected skips, 0 failures, including the full test job, three E2E shards, and win-x64/win-arm64 builds.

## Real behavior proof

Current-head regression tests map equal `OpenClaw Windows Tray` display names to distinct visible titles while retaining their original routing keys. Coverage also proves multi-segment and legacy-key collisions remain distinct and stable across channel filtering.

## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit.

WhatsApp rich inbound messages could bypass the configured inbound debounce window. Images, locations, quoted replies, and slow media preparation could trigger an auto-reply before nearby context arrived, so the agent could answer with incomplete context.

target.title: fix(nodes): keep Gateway connections healthy and consistent
target.body:
Closes #103079
Closes #103080
Supersedes #91466 and #78479

AI-assisted change; implementation and proof reviewed by the maintainer workflow.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issues where Gateway-connected nodes could remain falsely online after a missed WebSocket pong, invocation deadlines could disagree between the Gateway and node, and managed node services could lose password authentication or retain TLS settings from a previous endpoint.

These failures produced stale node state, false timeout results while work continued, and installed services that could not reconnect to the intended Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing 25-second protocol ping now terminates a peer after one missed pong and lets the normal close path release node state. Node invocations resolve one timer-safe timeout before dispatch, with zero consistently meaning no deadline.

Managed installs now persist password authentication through the existing file-backed environment path, safely round-trip systemd EnvironmentFile values, redact service credentials from JSON status, remove managed credentials during uninstall, and clear inherited TLS state only when the effective host or port changes. No new config, protocol, or environment-variable surface is introduced.

## User Impact

Half-open node connections are retired promptly, node invocation timeout results match the work running on the node, and password-authenticated managed nodes reconnect with the correct endpoint and certificate settings. Routine `openclaw node status --json` output remains safe to share.
